reasons: Both answers meet every rubric item in nearly the same way: a hedged range plus a padded window, a timed rehearsal on a restored copy multiplied by 1.5, a correct description of the full rewrite and index rebuild under ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, and an online migration built on a new column, a sync trigger and a batched backfill. A gives a ready-to-use statement for the meeting, while B adds useful points: parallel maintenance workers, WAL archiving and network bottlenecks, and a rule for choosing online or offline based on how much ID headroom is left. Each switchover script has a subtle flaw that makes neither clearly better: A leaves the old nextval default on id_old, and B drops that default while id_old keeps NOT NULL.

A: Switchover leaves id_old with its nextval default, so each insert consumes two sequence values and id_old will eventually overflow the integer range
B: Switchover drops the default on id_old, but id_old keeps NOT NULL after the PK is dropped in PG16, so inserts would fail with a not-null violation
